properties.name: Pacific Ring of Fire Zone
properties.principle: Geology: the subduction zones round the Pacific, and the Sunda arc that Starcom counts with them, where oceanic plates go under their neighbours, making the trenches, the volcanic arcs and most of the world's great earthquakes. Its Sectors are arcs, each a corridor 400 km wide along its axis between volcanic front and trench, as Starcom's band is; neighbours share their cuts, and parts across the date line are split at it.

measures.antimeridian: Split at the antimeridian into a part either side of it (no ring crosses ±180); Starcom's own band stops short of it instead.

properties.name: Southern Andes
properties.character: Where the Nazca and Antarctic plates go under South America from Patagonia to the Pampean flat slab: the Southern and Austral volcanic zones, Chile's central valley and its cities, and the coast of the largest earthquake recorded (Valdivia, 1960).

properties.name: Central Andes
properties.character: The Andes' widest stretch, from the Pampean flat slab to the Huancabamba bend: the Atacama coast, the Central Volcanic Zone's high volcanoes behind Arica and Arequipa, and Peru's coast, where the flat slab silences the volcanoes but not the earthquakes.

properties.character: Ecuador's and Colombia's Andes and Pacific coast, from the Huancabamba bend to the Darién: the Northern Volcanic Zone's ice-capped volcanoes over Quito, the Gulf of Guayaquil, and the trench that broke in 1906.

properties.name: Middle America Arc
properties.character: The Cocos plate going under Central America and Mexico along the Middle America Trench: the Central American volcanic arc from Panama to Guatemala, and Mexico's Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt, oblique to the trench, from Popocatépetl to Colima.

properties.name: California and Cascadia
properties.character: Where the Ring runs along transform faults and one short subduction zone: the Gulf of California's spreading, the San Andreas through California, the Cascadia subduction zone and its Cascade volcanoes, and the Queen Charlotte-Fairweather faults up to Alaska.

properties.name: Alaska–Aleutian Arc
properties.character: The Pacific plate going under North America from the Yakutat block to the Commander Islands: south-central Alaska's 1964 rupture zone, the Alaska Peninsula's volcanoes and the Aleutian island chain across the date line; its ash crosses the North Pacific air routes.

properties.name: Kamchatka, Kuril and Japan Arcs
properties.character: The Pacific plate going under Kamchatka, the Kurils and northeast Japan along one trench, then the Philippine Sea plate under southwest Japan along the Nankai Trough: Kamchatka's volcanoes, the Kuril chain, and Japan from Hokkaido to Kyushu, where the 2011 Tohoku earthquake struck.

properties.name: Izu–Bonin–Mariana Arc
properties.character: The oceanic arc where the Pacific plate goes under the Philippine Sea plate, south from the Izu peninsula: the Izu and Bonin islands, Iōtō, the Mariana Islands and Guam, above the deepest trench on Earth.

properties.name: Ryukyu, Taiwan and Philippine Arcs
properties.character: The Philippine Sea plate's western edge from the Tokara Strait to the Molucca Sea: the Ryukyu arc, Taiwan's collision, Luzon, the Visayas and Mindanao between two trenches, and the Sangihe and Halmahera arcs.

properties.character: From New Guinea's Bird's Head to Vanuatu: the New Guinea ranges, the New Britain and Solomon arcs over their trenches, and the Vanuatu arc, where the Australian plate goes under the Pacific's islands.

properties.character: The Indo-Australian plate going under Sundaland from Aceh to the Banda Sea: Sumatra's west coast and the 2004 rupture, the Sunda Strait, Java's and Bali's volcanoes, and the Banda arc's islands curving north to Banda Api.

properties.name: Tonga–Kermadec Arc and New Zealand
properties.character: The Pacific plate going under the Australian plate from Tonga to New Zealand's North Island along the Tonga, Kermadec and Hikurangi trenches, then the Alpine Fault across the South Island to Fiordland; across the date line.
